m8-a08.note: Isolated grader instance, fixture shortened digest config (120 s period), six seeded personas, every client closed before the period boundary. Exactly one digest per active user for the watched period. The Alice-analogue counts were exactly {newFollowers:1, newPostsInFollowing:1, unreadMessages:1, unreadChats:1}. A deliberately discriminating persona with 3 unread messages across 2 chats produced {unreadMessages:3, unreadChats:2}, so the two counters are genuinely distinct. A tombstoned message did not inflate any count.

m8-a09.note: The inert persona received zero digest payloads in any period. The message-sending-only persona also received none, consistent with the emit guard.

m8-a10.note: The following period (periodEnd +120 s) with no new activity emitted zero rows for any of the six personas, while the prior period's single row for the Alice-analogue remained exactly one.

m8-a11.note: The backend was SIGTERMed and restarted 35 s before the period boundary (mid-period, confirmed by timestamps). After restart exactly one digest per active user for that period and zero for inactive users. A second restart after the digests had already been written added zero rows, so the schema once[principal,periodEnd] key plus the worker idempotency-key ledger both hold.

m8-a12.note: Three messages were sent in a chat the target user is not a member of. The target's digest reported unreadMessages 1 / unreadChats 1 - only its own chat. The non-member chat's own member correctly got unreadMessages 3 / unreadChats 1. Structurally, the job runs "as p.principal" over members where .principal = viewer.
